referencePatternsToCopy.label: Event detail and RSVP flow
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy an event detail layout: title, date/time, location, host, capacity/status chip, attendee context, RSVP action, and confirmation state.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material navigation and information architecture
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Apple HIG navigation and content organization
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Make navigation predictable, content-centered, and appropriate for the user’s current task.

findings.title: Generic workflow/action-surface language remains visible across primary screens
findings.description: Current screenshots still show production-blocking phrases such as "Use this surface", "Decision", and "Decide what to save" across unrelated communities. This makes screens feel like a workflow framework or QA harness instead of a polished community product.
findings.requiredFix: Audit every affected screen and replace generic framework copy with community-specific product language. Each row must show the concrete object, relevant domain data, primary and alternate lifecycle actions, and result/receiver state in visible screenshots.

findings.title: Several workflows are mapped to the wrong product surface family
findings.description: Examples include Book Club search/AI digest rendered as an announcement composer, Soccer roster rendered as a generic member form, HOA document and facility flows rendered as generic form/payment surfaces, platform ad/no-fill rendered as member-channel update, and export preview rendered as request resolution. These mismatches prevent the UI from feeling like the intended community task.
findings.requiredFix: For each affected workflow, select the correct card-surface family and renderer: search/AI result with citations, roster table/list detail, document detail/download/access surface, reservation calendar/payment surface, ad disclosure/preference surface, and export/import preview wizard. Recapture screenshots proving the right surface is visible.

findings.title: Overall visual system still feels like hue-swapped template cards, not a mature product experience
findings.description: The current UI relies heavily on oversized same-shape cards, one-color palettes per community, large typography, and repeated chip rows. Some rows work, but the whole product still lacks enough hierarchy, density, navigation variety, and community-specific composition to meet a modern production bar.
findings.requiredFix: Introduce richer typed layouts for primary surfaces while keeping shared shell code: compact home sections, domain-specific detail pages/forms, tables/lists where appropriate, differentiated status/receipt panels, and more balanced typography/spacing/color. Recapture after screenshots and rerun the LLM review.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Does this feel like a modern production app for each community and persona, not merely implemented workflows?
visibleEvidence: Generic phrases such as Use this surface, Decision, and Decide what to save appear in current screenshots.

holisticQuestionAnswers.critique: The product is closer than early passes, and some rows are credible, but the overall experience still exposes implementation scaffolding and repeated templates. It should not pass production UX.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Replace generic workflow/template language and mismatched surfaces, then recapture full screenshots and rerun the fresh LLM review.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Are hierarchy, spacing, typography, color, and component variety shippable across the reviewed app?
visibleEvidence: The main pattern is still oversized full-screen cards with similar chip rows.
Community color changes often substitute for richer information architecture.

holisticQuestionAnswers.critique: The screens are readable, but not yet consistently modern or intentionally designed as a production app. They still look like a demo renderer in several places.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Introduce more varied domain-native layouts and denser, more purposeful hierarchy for primary screens.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Is information architecture centered on real user jobs and community content?

Book search/AI, soccer roster, HOA facility/document, platform ad, and export flows still show generic surface language or wrong surface families.
holisticQuestionAnswers.critique: The IA is moving toward community content, but the long tail of workflows is still generated from broad surface categories instead of purpose-built user tasks.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Map every workflow to its specific card surface and visible community object before rendering.

llmVisionReview.summary: Fresh pass-19 screenshot review fails B25. Full capture is current, and several screens are improved, but major product-UX issues remain: generic workflow/action language is still visible, some workflows use the wrong surface family, and the visual system remains too template/card-heavy to be called production-grade.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Does this feel like a modern production app for each community and persona, not merely implemented workflows?
visibleEvidence: Generic phrases such as Use this surface, Decision, and Decide what to save appear in current screenshots.
Several unrelated workflows share the same large action-surface template with only color/title changes.
Some workflows are visibly mapped to unrelated surface families.
holisticQuestionAnswers.critique: The product is closer than early passes, and some rows are credible, but the overall experience still exposes implementation scaffolding and repeated templates. It should not pass production UX.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Replace generic workflow/template language and mismatched surfaces, then recapture full screenshots and rerun the fresh LLM review.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Are hierarchy, spacing, typography, color, and component variety shippable across the reviewed app?
visibleEvidence: The main pattern is still oversized full-screen cards with similar chip rows.
Community color changes often substitute for richer information architecture.
Some home and action screens are visually one-note and low-density.
holisticQuestionAnswers.critique: The screens are readable, but not yet consistently modern or intentionally designed as a production app. They still look like a demo renderer in several places.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Introduce more varied domain-native layouts and denser, more purposeful hierarchy for primary screens.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Is information architecture centered on real user jobs and community content?
visibleEvidence: Garden RSVP and Masjid volunteer rows show concrete community objects.
Book search/AI, soccer roster, HOA facility/document, platform ad, and export flows still show generic surface language or wrong surface families.
holisticQuestionAnswers.critique: The IA is moving toward community content, but the long tail of workflows is still generated from broad surface categories instead of purpose-built user tasks.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Map every workflow to its specific card surface and visible community object before rendering.

findings.title: Generic workflow/action-surface language remains visible across primary screens
findings.description: Current screenshots still show production-blocking phrases such as "Use this surface", "Decision", and "Decide what to save" across unrelated communities. This makes screens feel like a workflow framework or QA harness instead of a polished community product.
findings.requiredFix: Audit every affected screen and replace generic framework copy with community-specific product language. Each row must show the concrete object, relevant domain data, primary and alternate lifecycle actions, and result/receiver state in visible screenshots.

findings.title: Several workflows are mapped to the wrong product surface family
findings.description: Examples include Book Club search/AI digest rendered as an announcement composer, Soccer roster rendered as a generic member form, HOA document and facility flows rendered as generic form/payment surfaces, platform ad/no-fill rendered as member-channel update, and export preview rendered as request resolution. These mismatches prevent the UI from feeling like the intended community task.
findings.requiredFix: For each affected workflow, select the correct card-surface family and renderer: search/AI result with citations, roster table/list detail, document detail/download/access surface, reservation calendar/payment surface, ad disclosure/preference surface, and export/import preview wizard. Recapture screenshots proving the right surface is visible.

findings.title: Overall visual system still feels like hue-swapped template cards, not a mature product experience
findings.description: The current UI relies heavily on oversized same-shape cards, one-color palettes per community, large typography, and repeated chip rows. Some rows work, but the whole product still lacks enough hierarchy, density, navigation variety, and community-specific composition to meet a modern production bar.
findings.requiredFix: Introduce richer typed layouts for primary surfaces while keeping shared shell code: compact home sections, domain-specific detail pages/forms, tables/lists where appropriate, differentiated status/receipt panels, and more balanced typography/spacing/color. Recapture after screenshots and rerun the LLM review.
